Privacy Policy

Effective — 28 July 2026

The short version

We are a small independent publication, not an advertising business. We do not sell your data, we do not share it with advertisers, and there are no third-party tracking or advertising cookies on this site.

We do measure how the site is read, and we do it ourselves rather than handing it to an outside analytics company. For a signed-in reader, that measurement is per-person: we can see which pages your account opened and roughly how long you spent on each. It is keyed to an internal account identifier, never to your email address, and only the site's administrators can see it.

If you would rather we did not hold any of it, write to contact@cricketimes.com and we will delete your account and its records.

This policy explains what Cricket Times collects, why, how long it is kept, and who can see it. Cricket Times is operated by Dreamers LLC, a Washington State limited liability company, at cricketimes.com. Dreamers LLC is the controller of the personal data described here. It sits alongside our Terms of Service.

1. What we collect

1.1 Account information

Much of the site can be read without an account. If you create one, we collect your email address, a password (which is hashed by Google Firebase Authentication — we never see or store the password itself), the display name you choose to appear beside your comments, and the access level your account holds. We also record when your account was created and when it last signed in.

1.2 Subscription information

If you subscribe, payment is taken by Stripe, our payment processor. We never receive or store your card number. What we hold is the status of your subscription — whether it is active, cancelled, or lapsed — together with the identifiers Stripe gives us so the two systems can refer to the same subscription. Stripe processes your payment details under its own privacy policy.

1.3 The newsletter

The newsletter is separate from your account, and subscribing to it is entirely voluntary. If you sign up we collect your email address and, if you give it, your first name. These are used for one thing: sending you summaries of what has been published on Cricket Times.

Newsletter subscriptions are stored and sent by MailerLite, our email service provider, under its own privacy policy. MailerLite is based in the European Union. Signing up to the newsletter does not create a Cricket Times account; if you also hold an account, the email address on it is held separately by us as account data, as described in section 1.1.

You can unsubscribe at any time using the link at the foot of any newsletter email, or by writing to contact@cricketimes.com. We action unsubscribe and deletion requests promptly, and unsubscribing from the newsletter does not affect your account or subscription.

1.4 How the site is read (engagement analytics)

We measure how the site is used, so that we can tell which writing is worth continuing and which parts of the site nobody opens. This measurement is built by us and runs on our own Firebase infrastructure. It is not Google Analytics, and no analytics vendor, advertising network, or data broker receives any of it.

For a signed-in reader, the measurement is tied to that account. We collect:

What Detail
Page path The path of the page you opened — for example /oracle.html. Anything after the ? in a web address is never recorded.
Time and duration When you arrived, how long the visit lasted, and how much of that time you were actually reading rather than idle. Time is counted in short intervals and only while the page is visible and you have interacted with it recently.
Per-page reading history For an account, a list of which specific pages that account has opened and how long was spent on each. This is individual reading behaviour, not just an aggregate count, and we describe it plainly here because that distinction matters.
Return visits How often an account comes back, and when it last did.
Sign-in records A record of each sign-in: the account's email address, the page you arrived on, and a timestamp set by our server.

Two deliberate limits are worth naming. First, the reading measurement above — the pages, the timings, the history — is keyed to an internal account identifier, a random string issued by Firebase, and not to your email address. The sign-in log is the one exception: it is written against the account's email address, because its purpose is to show us who signed in rather than what they read. Second, we do not follow you across other websites, we do not buy or receive data about you from anyone else, and we do not build an advertising or interest profile from any of this.

1.5 Comments, reactions, and submissions

If you post a comment we store its text, your display name, your account identifier, and the time it was posted. Reactions store the fact that your account reacted, so the count is right. If you submit an article as a contributor, we store the submission and anything you upload with it.

1.6 Technical records

Our hosting and server infrastructure is provided by Google Firebase and Google Cloud, which keeps operational logs — including IP addresses, request times, and browser and device information — as an ordinary part of serving and securing a website. Google handles this under its Firebase privacy documentation. We use these logs for security, abuse prevention, and debugging. We do not use them to identify readers or to work out where you are.

1.7 Identifiers in subscriber content

Content served to a signed-in account may carry an identifier tying that copy to the account it was served to. It exists for one purpose: if subscriber material is republished in breach of our Terms of Service, it lets us establish where the copy came from. It is not used for advertising, profiling, or any other purpose, and it is derived from your account identifier rather than from anything about you personally.

2. Why we collect it, and on what basis

Purpose Basis (UK/EU GDPR)
Running your account and giving you the access you hold Performance of our contract with you
Taking payment and managing subscriptions Performance of our contract; legal obligation for tax and accounting records
Understanding how the site is read, so we can decide what to publish Our legitimate interest in running and improving an independent publication
Keeping the site secure, and enforcing our Terms Our legitimate interest in protecting the site and our work
Sending emails you asked for Your consent, which you can withdraw at any time

If you are in the UK or EU and you object to the analytics described in section 1.4 on the basis of your particular situation, write to us and we will stop measuring your account and delete what we hold for it. You do not have to give a reason beyond that.

3. How long we keep it

  • Detailed activity records — the underlying event log, in which each page you opened is a separate entry with its own timestamp — are kept for 90 days and then deleted automatically. Deletion runs as a background job rather than on the stroke of the ninetieth day, so an entry may survive a short time past its expiry before it is removed.
  • Summary figures derived from them — including, for each account, a daily record of which pages it opened, how many times, and how long was spent on each — are kept while your account exists, and are deleted with it. We want to be plain that these summaries outlive the detailed records they are built from: what expires at 90 days is the moment-by-moment trail, not the daily per-page picture.
  • Sign-in records — kept while your account is open, and deleted when you close it.
  • Account and subscription records — kept while your account is open, and deleted when you close it, except where we must keep payment and tax records for longer by law.
  • Comments — kept while posted. If you close your account you can ask us to remove your comments as well; say so when you write to us.
  • Newsletter subscriptions — held by MailerLite until you unsubscribe or ask for deletion.
  • Published contributor articles — kept in the archive indefinitely, as any publication keeps what it has published.

4. Who can see it

Internally: only the site's administrators. The analytics collections are written by our servers rather than by your browser, and the security rules that govern them permit reading only by an administrator account. Cricket Times is a very small operation, and in practice that means the people who run it.

Externally: we do not sell personal information, and we do not share it for advertising. The only third parties that handle your data are the service providers we need in order to operate — Google Firebase and Google Cloud (hosting, authentication, database, and email delivery for account messages), Stripe (subscription payments), and MailerLite (the newsletter) — and each only to the extent needed to provide that service. We may also disclose information where we are legally required to, or where it is necessary to establish or defend a legal claim.

Cricket Times is operated from the United States and the data described here is processed there. If you are in the UK or EU, that is a transfer outside your jurisdiction; our providers operate under standard contractual clauses and their own transfer frameworks.

5. Cookies and local storage

There are no advertising cookies on this site, and no third-party tracking on the pages where you read. What we use ourselves is strictly functional: a session cookie and a token that keep you signed in, and a small amount of browser storage that remembers things like whether you have already reacted to a comment and whether this visit has already been counted as a sign-in. Clearing your browser storage signs you out; it does not delete anything we hold.

One exception is worth naming plainly. The pages that carry an email signup form load that form from MailerLite rather than serving it ourselves. To render it, MailerLite's code contacts MailerLite's servers, requests a web font from Google, and may store an identifier in your browser. This happens only on those pages, and only because the form is there — it is not used to follow you, and none of it runs on the pages where you read. We intend to replace these forms with a version that loads no third-party code at all, and we will update this section when that is done.

6. Your rights

You can ask us to:

  • tell you what we hold about you, and give you a copy;
  • correct anything that is wrong;
  • delete your account and the records attached to it;
  • stop measuring your reading, while leaving your account and subscription in place;
  • stop sending you email.

Write to contact@cricketimes.com. We will action requests promptly and will not charge you or make you give a reason. Depending on where you live you may also have a right to complain to a data-protection authority — in the UK, the Information Commissioner's Office — and we would rather you came to us first, but that is your right either way.

We do not discriminate against anyone for exercising these rights: your subscription, price, and access stay exactly the same.

7. Children

Cricket Times is not directed at children under 13, and we do not knowingly collect personal information from them. If you believe a child has given us personal data, contact us and we will delete it.

8. Changes to this policy

We may update this policy. The version on this page is the one in force, and the effective date at the top changes when it does. Where a change materially affects how we handle your data, we will make reasonable efforts to tell account holders rather than relying on you to re-read the page.

This policy describes what Cricket Times does today. We currently run no advertising and no third-party analytics service. If that changes — if we introduce advertising on the freely available pages, or bring in an outside analytics provider — we will update this page and say so before it starts, and we will put in place whatever consent mechanism the law where you live requires. We will not quietly begin doing something this page says we do not do.

9. Contact

Questions about this policy, or any request under section 6:

Email: contact@cricketimes.com
